text:
A solution of two components containing
$n_{1}$ moles of the $1^{st}$ component and $n_{2}$ moles of
the $2^{nd}$ component is prepared. $M_{1}$ and $M_{2}$ are
the molecular weights of component 1 and 2
respectively. If d is the density of the solution
in $g mL^{–1}, C_{2}$ is the molarity and $x_{2}$ is the mole
fraction of the $2^{nd}$ component, then $C_{2}$ can be
expressed as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of the solution $=n_{1}M_{1}+n_{2}M_{2}$ g, so its volume $=\dfrac{n_{1}M_{1}+n_{2}M_{2}}{d}$ mL.

Molarity of component 2:

$C_{2}=\dfrac{n_{2}\times 1000}{V(\text{mL})}=\dfrac{1000\qquad dn_{2}}{n_{1}M_{1}+n_{2}M_{2}}$

Dividing numerator and denominator by $(n_{1}+n_{2})$, with $x_{2}=\dfrac{n_{2}}{n_{1}+n_{2}}$ and $\dfrac{n_{1}}{n_{1}+n_{2}}=1-x_{2}$:

$C_{2}=\dfrac{1000\qquad dx_{2}}{(1-x_{2})M_{1}+x_{2}M_{2}}=\dfrac{1000\qquad dx_{2}}{M_{1}+x_{2}(M_{2}-M_{1})}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

text:
For the reaction

$Fe_{2}N(s) +$ $\frac{3}{2}H_{2}(g)$ ⇌ $2Fe(s) + NH_{3}(g)$

the correct relation between $K_{C}$ and $K_{p}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the correct relationship between the equilibrium constants $K_{C}$ and $K_{p}$ for the reaction:

$\text{Fe}_{2}\text{N(s)}+\frac{3}{2}\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}⇌2\text{Fe(s)}+\text{NH}_{3}\text{(g)}$

First, consider the general relationship between $K_{C}$ and $K_{p}$:

$K_{p}=K_{C}(RT)^{\Delta n}$

where $\Delta n$ is the change in the number of moles of gas between the products and the reactants, $R$ is the ideal gas constant, and $T$ is the temperature in Kelvin.

For the given reaction, calculate $\Delta n$:

Moles of gas in products: $NH_{3(g)} = 1$ mole

Moles of gas in reactants: $\frac{3}{2}$ $H_{2(g)} = 1.5$ moles

Therefore:

$\Delta n=1-1.5=-0.5$

Substitute this value into the equation relating $K_{C}$ and $K_{p}$:

$K_{p}=K_{C}(RT)^{-0.5}$

Rearrange to express $K_{C}$:

$K_{C}=K_{p}(RT)^{0.5}$

Thus, the correct option is:

Option A: $K_{C}=K_{p}(RT)^{1/2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

text:
The major products of the following reaction are :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Potassium tert-butoxide is a bulky base, so E2 elimination of the mesylate removes a proton from the less hindered terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ group and gives the Hofmann alkene:

$(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OSO}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$

Ozonolysis with oxidative work-up ($\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$, then $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$) cleaves the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ bond and oxidises each fragment to the carboxylic acid:

$(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{HCOOH}$

The Zaitsev alkene $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, which would give acetone and acetic acid, is the minor product with this hindered base.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The diene has two isolated C=C bonds; each adds one HBr through the more stable carbocation. Number the ring with C-1 carrying $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (double bond C-1=C-2) and C-4 carrying $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ (double bond C-4=C-5).

C-1=C-2: $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ adds to C-2, giving the tertiary carbocation at C-1, so Br goes to C-1 (Markovnikov).

C-4=C-5: a carbocation at C-4 would be strongly destabilised by the –I and –M effects of $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$, so $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ adds to C-4 and the carbocation forms at C-5, which takes Br.

The product carries Br and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ on C-1, Br on C-5 and $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ on C-4. Renumbered by IUPAC rules it is 1,3-dibromo-1-methyl-4-nitrocyclohexane: the second Br sits on the carbon next to $\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ and two carbons away from $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{Br})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

text:
The major product obtained from the following
reaction is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Hg}{}^{2+}$/$\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ hydrates the C≡C bond: the electrophile adds so that positive charge develops on the alkyne carbon that can stabilise it better, water attacks that carbon, and the enol formed tautomerises to a ketone.

The alkyne carbon bonded to the p-methoxyphenyl ring is stabilised by the +M effect of $-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$, whereas the carbon bonded to the p-nitrophenyl ring is destabilised by the –M and –I effects of $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$.

So OH, and finally C=O, ends up on the carbon bonded to the p-methoxyphenyl ring, and the other alkyne carbon becomes $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$:

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}{}^{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}\longrightarrow \mathrm{O}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$

The product is 1-(4-methoxyphenyl)-2-(4-nitrophenyl)ethan-1-one; the $-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ group is not affected under these conditions. Option (A) would need the positive charge on the carbon next to the nitrophenyl ring.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

text:
The variation of equilibrium constant with
temperature is given below :

  
    Temperature
    Equilibrium Constant
  

  
    $T_{1} = 25^{o}C$
    $K_{1} = 10$
  
  
    $T_{2} = 100^{o}C$
    $K_{2} = 100$
  

The values of $\Delta H^{o}$, $\Delta G^{o}$ at 
$T_{1}$ and $\Delta G^{o}$ at $T_{2}$
(in kJ mol$^{–1})$ respectively, are close to :
[Use
$R = 8.314 J K^{–1}$ mol$^{–1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
ln $\left [\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}\right ]$ = $\frac{\Delta H^{\circ }}{R}\left \{\frac{1}{T_{1}}-\frac{1}{T_{2}}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ ln(10) = $\frac{\Delta H^{\circ }}{R}\left \{\frac{1}{298}-\frac{1}{373}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta H^{\circ }$ = 28.37 kJ/mol

$\Delta G^{o} = –RT \ln  K$

$T_{1} = 25^{o}C K_{1} = 10$

$\Delta G^{o}$ at $T_{1} = –8.314 × 298 × 2.303 × \log  10$

= –5.71 kJ/mol

$\Delta G^{o}$ at $T_{2} = –8.314 × 373 × 2.303 × \log (100)$

= –14.29 kJ/mol

text:
Potassium chlorate is prepared by the
electrolysis of KCl in basic solution

$6OH^{-} + Cl^{-}$ $\to$ ClO$_{3}^{-} + 3H_{2}O + 6e^{-}$

If only 60% of the current is utilized in the
reaction, the time (rounded to the nearest hour)
required to produce 10 g of KClO$_{3}$ using a
current of $2 A is_________$.

(Given : F = 96,500 C mol$^{–1}$; molar mass of
KCIO$_{3} = 122 g$ mol$^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For synthesis of 1 mole of  ClO$_{3}^{-} , 6F$ of charge
is required.

$\therefore$ To synthesise
$\frac{10}{122}$ moles of KClO$_{3}$,

Charge required = $\frac{10}{122}\times 6$ F

$\frac{10}{122}\times 6=\frac{2\times t(hr)\times 3600}{96500}\times \frac{60}{100}$

$\Rightarrow$ t(hr) = $\frac{965\times 100}{122\times 2\times 36}$ = 10.98 hr $\simeq$ 11 Hr
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

text:
The elevation of boiling point of 0.10 m
aqueous CrCl$_{3}$.xNH$_{3}$ solution is two times that
of 0.05 m aqueous CaCl$_{2}$ solution. The value of
x is $______$.

[Assume 100% ionisation of the complex and
CaCl$_{2}$, coordination number of Cr as 6, and that
all $NH_{3}$ molecules are present inside the
coordination sphere]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molality of CaCl$_{2}$ solution = 0.05 m

$\Delta T_{b} = i K_{b} m = 3 × K_{b} × 0.05 = 0.15 K_{b}$

Molality of CrCl$_{3}$.xNH$_{3} = 0.10 m$

$\Delta T_{b}^{'} = i K_{b}$ $\times$ 0.10

Given, $\Delta T_{b}^{'} = 2\Delta T_{b}$

$\Rightarrow$ $i K_{b}$ $\times$ 0.10 = 2 $\times$ $0.15 K_{b}$

$\Rightarrow$ i = 3

Co-ordination number of Cr is 6.

[$Cr(NH_{3}$
$)_{x}.Cl_{6-x}$]$Cl_{3-6+x}$ $\to$ [$Cr(NH_{3}$
$)_{x}Cl$] $+ (3-6+x)Cl^{–}$

 i = 3 = 1 + 3 - 6 + x

$\Rightarrow$ x = 5
